title: Exploring the distributional implications of targeted residential electrification in California - Nature Energy
text:
AbstractResidential electrification can reduce emissions but its household economics remain uncertain in regions with high electricity prices. Here we report a household-level analysis of 21,609 gas-heated homes in California, evaluating costs, emissions and equity under alternative end-use, tariff and rollout scenarios. Across modelled scenarios, only 15% of households achieve positive net present values. Cost-effectiveness is substantially higher for homes with existing air conditioning: 53–72% break even when electrifying space heating, compared with fewer than 10% of homes without it. Lower-volumetric tariffs improve bill savings under full electrification for many households, although outcomes vary by assistance-programme enrolment. Modelled income-targeted rebates substantially improve outcomes for low- and moderate-income households. Targeting areas with older gas infrastructure yields emissions reductions comparable to higher-income-first adoption but a larger aggregate private net present value shortfall. Lower installation costs, targeted incentives and tariff reform are therefore central to equitable, widespread residential electrification across high-cost electricity regions.

Data availability

Methodological descriptions and non-confidential summaries sufficient to interpret and reproduce the analytical framework are provided within the Article and its Supplementary Information. The household-level metered gas and electricity data used in this study were obtained under a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) with Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) and therefore cannot be shared publicly. As portions of the analysis code directly reference confidential data structures and variables defined by the NDA, the full codebase cannot be released. Please contact the PG&E Energy Data Request Program (https://pge-energydatarequest.com/) for access to the data.
Code availability

Portions of the analysis code directly reference confidential data structures and variables defined under the PG&E NDA. As a result, the full codebase cannot be released.
